evidence.text: IEEPA tariff refunds probably kept landing in Buckle's Aug-Oct quarter. In Q2 (May-Jul) Buckle booked a 65bp merchandise-margin benefit from refunds (about $2.1m), and that was all of its year-to-date refund (35bp of 26-week sales); Q1 said no material funds had arrived. CBP's Phase 1 refund system opened 2026-04-20 with payment 60-90 days after acceptance, which puts the bulk of payments in July-September. Peers with Aug-Oct or Jun-Aug quarters booked large refunds: TJX Q3 FY27 (to Oct 31) had a $0.05 net EPS benefit, and Levi Q3 (to Aug 30) had 370bp of gross margin. Consensus EPS of $0.88, down 9% y/y, does not visibly include a refund. A $2-4m refund is worth about $0.03-0.06 EPS, 3-7% of the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY2026 (2026-08-21) beat $0.87 vs $0.81, with the refund disclosed in the release: +2.74%. Q1 FY2026 (2026-05-29) headline beat driven by a $19.1m one-off litigation settlement while gross margin fell 50bp: -9.13%. This name has sold a one-off-driven beat when the underlying margin was weak.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market expected a refund, consensus EPS would not sit 9% below last year on sales that are now known to be 2.6% higher, and UBS would not be citing gross margin contraction. Buckle discloses refunds only in percentage terms after the fact and has no receivable or guidance on them, so no estimate can model it. It is still a one-off with no path to guidance (the company gives none), and investors may strip it out.
evidence.independence: Different sources point the same way: TJX Q3 FY27 8-K ($0.05 tariff-refund benefit, quarter to Oct 31) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm; Levi Q3 2026 8-K (370bp from refunds) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000094845/000009484526000048/exhibit991-3q2026pressrele.htm; NRF on Phase 1 timing (2026-04-30) https://nrf.com/blog/ieepa-tariff-refunds-are-moving-forward. These are proxies: Buckle itself has not said more refunds are pending.

evidence.text: Inventory rose 13.3% y/y to $161.4m at 2026-08-01 (vs $142.5m), against Q2 sales up only 4.6%, and the markdown reserve rose to $9.2m from $8.6m at year-end. Sales then decelerated through Q3: August comps +1.6%, September +0.5%, October -0.5%, quarter +0.6%. Last year's Q3 merchandise margin already fell 10bp, and Q2 FY2026 merchandise margin was up only about 45bp excluding the refund. Carrying that inventory into a softer quarter raises markdown risk to merchandise margin, which is the line the stock sold off on in Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY2026: gross margin -50bp (merchandise -10bp, occupancy -40bp), stock -9.13% despite a headline beat. Q2 FY2026: gross margin +40bp, stock +2.74%. Gross margin is the line this name trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is down 11% in 20 days, UBS expects gross margin contraction, and consensus EBIT is down 8.5%. What is not visibly priced is the inventory build specifically: no preview found mentions it. If it were priced we would expect a deeper skew than +3.2 and estimate cuts citing inventory. Some of the build may be new stores (451 vs 442) and earlier receipts ahead of tariffs, which would reduce the markdown risk.
evidence.independence: Monthly comps come from separate company releases: https://www.rttnews.com/3697505/buckle-september-sales-rise-2-2.aspx and https://finviz.com/news/416668/the-buckle-inc-reports-october-2026-net-sales. The inventory and margin figures share the Q2 10-Q/release with the refund finding but rest on different lines.

evidence.text: SG&A deleverage is the other margin swing, and it sits inside consensus. Q2 SG&A rose to 30.4% of sales from 29.0% (+140bp: marketing, store labor, health insurance, supplies) on +2.1% comps, partly cushioned by 35bp of lower incentive accruals, and buying/distribution/occupancy deleveraged 70bp. Q3 comps were only +0.6%, so deleverage likely persists or widens. A simple model (gross margin -50 to -80bp, SG&A +120 to +140bp) gives operating margin of about 17.2-17.5%, around $57m, against $56.05m consensus EBIT. That is roughly in line, with a slight downside tail if deleverage exceeds Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY2026 operating margin fell 100bp to 17.4%, yet the stock rose 2.74% on the EPS beat. Q1 FY2026's underlying SG&A rose 145bp excluding the settlement, and the stock fell 9.13%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus EBIT already implies about 190bp less operating margin. It is filed because the size of the deleverage on a +0.6% comp is the second unknown of the print. A worse number would only surprise if SG&A growth stepped above Q2's 9.6%.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2 10-Q with findings 1 and 2, on a different line. The consensus EBIT comes from https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982.

Headline Q3 revenue is therefore likely about $770-790m, against a $740-753m consensus, unless analysts already folded it in.

evidence.why_not_priced: Most Q3 consensus figures ($740.3m, $745.9m) sit on the ex-acquisition guide midpoint of $739m. If Airtable were in them they would read about $775m+. Only Chartmill's $753m hints at partial inclusion. A headline beat that is inorganic is usually recognised as such by holders, which is why it is sized small.
evidence.independence: The ARR figure comes from a separate source, the SaaStr deal analysis (https://www.saastr.com/airtable-just-sold-for-2-25b-at-2-7x-arr-it-raised-1-4b-and-was-once-worth-11-7b/), and the guide exclusion from the company's Q2 release p.4. evidence.text: The Q4/FY outlook given on 11-20 will be the first to include Airtable (a full Q4, roughly $115-125m) and Miro (closed 2026-10-26, about 66 days at about $600m ARR, roughly $100-110m), plus Airtable's September. The FY2026 revenue guide therefore resets mechanically from $2.78-2.82bn to roughly $3.0-3.06bn, above the ~$2.90bn mean consensus whose shortfall drove the Q2 sell-off. On the existing perimeter, the old FY guide implies only about $755m for Q4 (FY $2.80bn less Q1 $601m, Q2 $704m and Q3 $739m), below the ~$840m the street's $2.88-2.90bn implied.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide is the line this stock traded on last time: a FY revenue midpoint of $2.80bn against $2.895bn consensus sent it down about 16-17% on 2026-08-13 despite the quarterly beat (finviz 381910; https://www.finanzaonline.com/notizie/bending-spoons-deraglia-post-conti-cosa-non-ha-convinto-wall-street).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FY2027 consensus of $4.26bn (stockanalysis, 2026-11-16) shows models carry the deals forward, and the FY2026 consensus range reaches $3.1bn. But the FY2026 mean is still $2.90bn and the BofA note says the buy-side bar is below guidance, with put skew at +14 and P/C OI at 4.3. If a raised outlook were expected, the put premium would not be this large and the stock would not have fallen 5.6% in November. What decides the sign is the ex-deal Q4: the market sees the headline raise, and the organic core either confirms the ~$755m implied Q4 or beats it.
evidence.independence: Airtable timing is from the company completion release (finviz 389082). Miro EV and ARR come from the deal announcement (https://finviz.com/news/390888/bending-spoons-agrees-to-acquire-miro-at-136-billion-enterprise-value). Q1 revenue of $601.3m comes from the F-1 coverage (https://fortune.com/2026/06/08/bending-spoons-italian-aol-evernote-wetransfer-files-us-ipo/). Both deal releases say the company 'expects to incorporate [the business] into its outlook when it next reports financial results'.

evidence.text: Organic revenue growth slowed from 6% in Q1 to 3% in Q2 2026, with Remini and Splice revenue declining and only Tractive and WeTransfer growing (company release). Management cited market saturation and competition at Remini. If the trend continued, Q3 organic growth lands around 0-2%, and the ex-deal Q4 guide implied by the old FY range (~$755m) suggests the core is not re-accelerating.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 deceleration from 6% to 3% was cited alongside the FY guide as a cause of the ~16-17% fall on 2026-08-13 (https://www.saastr.com/5-interesting-learnings-from-bending-spoons-at-2-8-billion-in-revenue-126-growth-3-organic-growth-and-1-08-billion-of-arr-bought-in-37-days).
evidence.why_not_priced: The deceleration itself is public. What is not known is whether Q3 organic growth turned negative. Organic growth is not a consensus line, and the Airtable and Miro headline will mask it until the release footnote is read. Nobody can trade it ahead of the release, and the put skew is consistent with part of this fear already being in the price.
evidence.independence: BofA (2026-11-16) puts about 30% of the revenue run rate as highly exposed to AI disruption, which points the same way (https://finimize.com/content/bofa-thinks-bending-spoons-ai-fears-are-getting-priced-in-early).
